title: Andouille Po Boy Rolls for the Crew
displayTitle: Andouille Po Boy Rolls for the Crew
seoTitle: Andouille Po Boy Rolls for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Po boy night—grilled andouille, Cajun remoulade, New Orleans hall energy
subtitle: Grilled andouille, remoulade, and crispy baguette for ten
description: Andouille sausage splits and grills until charred, piles on toasted baguette with lettuce, tomato, and spicy remoulade for ten po boys.

steps.title: Build remoulade
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, Creole mustard, hot sauce, and minced celery. Chill until service. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Split andouille
steps.instruction: Split sausage links lengthwise—not all the way through—so they lay flat on the grill. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill andouille
steps.instruction: Grill split andouille cut-side down at 400°F 5 minutes, flip, grill 5–7 minutes until charred and 165°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold proteins at safe temp
steps.instruction: Slice on bias and hold covered at 170°F in hotel pans. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Toast baguettes
steps.instruction: Butter baguette splits and toast on griddle at 375°F until crisp, 2–3 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep fixings
steps.instruction: Shred lettuce and slice tomatoes. Keep cold until build. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build po boys
steps.instruction: Spread remoulade on toasted rolls. Layer andouille, lettuce, tomato, and extra remoulade. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: One po boy per firefighter with pickle chips. Wrap in parchment for messy hands. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Split andouille lays flat—whole links roll on the grates.
Toast rolls well—soft bread collapses under juicy sausage.
Remoulade on both cut sides of roll prevents dry bites.
tonightSpread: Andouille po boy rolls with remoulade and pickles.
Red beans and rice if you want a full NOLA plate.
leftovers: Sliced andouille into jambalaya next shift.
Po boy halves re-toast on griddle.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Andouille po boys are distinct from pulled pork or brisket sandwiches. Sausage grills fast, holds at 170°F, and builds on toasted rolls at the line.
mealPrepNotes: Split and grill andouille at 400°F, 10–12 minutes. Hold sliced sausage at 170°F up to 40 minutes. Toast rolls at 375°F. Build to order.
